clusters.label: Model target UI on in-app example
clusters.family: Worked example to model the implementation on
clusters.definition: The design system ships a story that depicts the very screen or widget the agent is building or changing (a cart row, an action stack, a step indicator, a side panel, an in-app dialog). The agent loads it to see how the design system itself composes that UI - which props, layout, sibling elements, labels and emphasis - so its own code can mirror it. The story was the vehicle because its name or listed description names the target UI, its siblings are single-prop demos or tests, and its source had not yet been shown.
clusters.include: Open 'how does the reference build / arrange / configure this' questions put to an app-context example not yet seen in source: placing and wiring a control in a row, stacking and distinguishing primary vs secondary actions, how a step indicator combines the bar with text and a label, panel or dialog content arrangement, overall form sectioning; also checking finished work against the example.
clusters.exclude: Same stories probed for one native-HTML mechanism (form element, submit control, name/type/autocomplete) -> k05; rule: if most of the aspects the need lists are native form mechanics it is k05, otherwise k01. Loaded only to learn WHICH component the design system uses for the job, with no how-to-configure part -> k10 (any 'and how is it set up / laid out' clause keeps it in k01). Example whose source the trigger/cue says was already printed or seen, loaded again -> k02. Catalogue of styles rather than an in-context example -> k14.

clusters.label: Re-load seen example for hidden markup
clusters.family: Worked example to model the implementation on
clusters.definition: The agent had already been shown this example story, but what it saw was terse - typically a one-line call to a helper component that hides the real markup or API call. It loads the story on its own hoping the single-story view exposes what the helper renders: the composition, props, labels or calls behind it. The story remains the vehicle because it is still the only example of the wanted usage.
clusters.include: Composition or usage questions where the trigger or cue says this story's source had already been printed or seen (full docs dump of every story, 'already shown', 're-fetched alone for fuller source', 'what does the hidden helper/wrapper render'), whether the story is an app-context example or a component's own demo.
clusters.exclude: First-time load of an app-context example (listed by name/description, 'without source') -> k01. Re-load of a behaviour-named test story to confirm a fact -> k04. Sole story (re)loaded in search of when-to-use guidance rather than markup -> k11. After the example proved opaque, turning to a DIFFERENT, structural story -> k12.

clusters.label: Story name asserts unstated native behaviour
clusters.family: Behaviour the props table leaves unstated
clusters.definition: The props table is silent on a native-HTML behaviour the fix depends on: a default attribute value, whether it can be overridden, whether refs and extra attributes are forwarded. A story - usually a test story - is listed whose name states exactly that behaviour, so the agent loads it to confirm the fact and see whether there is a way around it. The name alone made it the vehicle; no other listed story touches the topic.
clusters.include: 'Does X default to / always render / forward ...' questions answered by a story named after that behaviour and known only by name or listed without source (e.g. a default button type, ref-and-props forwarding, pass-through of native attributes).
clusters.exclude: Same story when the trigger/cue says its source was already in a full docs dump -> k04. Same question put to a story that does not name the behaviour (Anatomy, Variants, Class Name, the last unseen story) -> k06, or to an app-context example -> k05. Behaviour-named stories about announcements, roles or ranges for assistive technology -> k09. Behaviour-named stories about what happens at min/max -> k07.

clusters.label: Re-load printed test story to confirm
clusters.family: Behaviour the props table leaves unstated
clusters.definition: Same knowledge as k03 - a native default stated in a test story's name - but the docs output had already printed that story's source among all the others. The agent loads it again by itself to isolate it from a very long page, double-check the fact, or see whether the story says anything more.
clusters.include: Items whose trigger or cue says the docs had printed every story (or this story) in full and the behaviour-named test story was then loaded alone.
clusters.exclude: Story known only by name or listed without source -> k03. Re-loads aimed at markup hidden behind a helper -> k02.

clusters.label: Probe in-app example for form wiring
clusters.family: Behaviour the props table leaves unstated
clusters.definition: The agent suspects a native form mechanism is missing or undocumented (a real form element, a submit control or type, name/type/autocomplete on fields) and the component docs do not say how the design system handles it. It loads the design system's app-context example of that flow as evidence: does the sanctioned example contain the mechanism, and how is it wired? The story is the vehicle because it is the only one showing the components in the relevant real flow, where such a pattern would appear if one existed.
clusters.include: Targeted 'does the reference example wrap fields in a form / show a submit button or handler / pass type, name or autocomplete' probes of an app-context example, including follow-ups after a behaviour-named test story returned only a bare component.
clusters.exclude: Open-ended 'how is the example composed / laid out / styled' -> k01 (rule: if the need lists several aspects, count them; mostly sections, headings, error display, layout -> k01; mostly form element, submit, native attributes -> k05). The same native question put to a behaviour-named test story -> k03/k04, or to Anatomy / Variants / Class Name / the last unseen story -> k06.

clusters.label: Mine leftover stories for native hints
clusters.family: Behaviour the props table leaves unstated
clusters.definition: No story directly answers the undocumented native question (which element is rendered, a type/submit option, pass-through of native attributes), so the agent turns to an indirect story that might leak a hint. It picks the structural 'Anatomy' story, the one story still unseen, a variants catalogue or a className demo because that is the likeliest remaining place for the element and its attributes to show.
clusters.include: Native-attribute, rendered-element or submit-capability questions put to a story whose name does not state that behaviour, including when that story is the only one the component offers or the only one left unread.
clusters.exclude: Story name states the behaviour -> k03. App-context example probed for the mechanism -> k05. Anatomy loaded for parts, composition or basic wiring with no native-attribute question as the main clause -> k12. Variants loaded to pick a visual style -> k14. Class Name loaded in order to restyle or position -> k15.

clusters.label: Behaviour at limits named in story
clusters.family: Behaviour the props table leaves unstated
clusters.definition: The props table gives numeric bounds but not what the control does when it reaches them (disable, clamp, wrap, allow zero). The agent loads the story whose title states the boundary rule to learn that edge behaviour and judge whether it suits the intended use.
clusters.include: Questions about behaviour at min/max or other limits, answered by a story named after the rule rather than after a prop.
clusters.exclude: Using an in-context example to see which bounds are passed -> k01. Structural overview of the control -> k12. Behaviour-named stories about native attributes -> k03, about assistive technology -> k09.

clusters.label: Accessible-name prop and its wording
clusters.definition: The agent knows a control needs an accessible name and wants to know what the naming prop does and what wording the design system expects: what it names, how it is phrased, whether it is visible or name-only. It loads the story dedicated to that prop or rule (an aria-label story, a label story, an icon-only-needs-a-label story) because the type signature and the other stories give no example value.
clusters.include: Usage and wording of aria-label / label for a control or group, and rules for naming icon-only controls, via the story named after the naming prop or rule.
clusters.exclude: What the component itself emits or announces without caller input (roles, ranges, live regions, error wiring) -> k09. Labelling observed as one part of a whole in-context example -> k01.

clusters.label: Built-in assistive-technology semantics
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know what the component does on its own for assistive technology: how an error is announced, whether the error node is always mounted, what role and value range a progress bar reports. It loads the story (mostly test stories, once an Anatomy story described in ARIA terms) whose name or description states that accessibility behaviour, since props tables do not describe emitted ARIA.
clusters.include: Announcement mechanism, live-region / aria-describedby wiring, always-mounted error slot, reported range / role / ARIA of a component.
clusters.exclude: What text to put in a naming prop -> k08. How an in-context example labels a widget -> k01 (or k02 if already seen). Anatomy chosen for its parts, with assistive-technology wiring only a secondary clause -> k12. Native form behaviour such as a default type -> k03.

clusters.label: Intended use shown by in-app example
clusters.definition: The agent is deciding which component the design system intends for a job (the app uses two different controls for the same task) and has found no written guidance. It loads a component's app-context example purely as evidence of what the design system uses that component for.
clusters.include: 'What is this component used for in the app / is it the intended control there' questions answered by the component's in-app story, with no interest in how to configure it.
clusters.exclude: If the need also asks how the control is set up, laid out or wired in that example -> k01. Seeking when-to-use prose from a component's only story -> k11. Comparing controls by inspecting parts / anatomy -> k12.

clusters.label: Sole story mined for usage guidance
clusters.definition: Docs for the candidate components are bare and no guideline pages can be found, so the agent loads the component's single listed story as the last documented source, hoping the story-level view carries a description or when-to-use guidance. The story is the vehicle only because nothing else is available.
clusters.include: 'Does the only story say anything about when / where / how this should be used' loads, typically a lone 'Empty' or 'Anatomy' story after guidance searches failed.
clusters.exclude: Only story loaded for markup or usage wiring -> k12 (or k02 if the trigger says it was already seen). Only story loaded for native attributes -> k06. In-app example used as intended-use evidence -> k10.

clusters.label: Structural story for parts and wiring
clusters.definition: The agent needs the component's basic make-up - its parts and slots, what it renders, which props it takes, how value, handlers and labels are wired - usually because the docs are thin or the in-context example turned out to be an opaque helper. It loads the structural story ('Anatomy', or one named after the underlying control) because that name promises an overview of the whole component rather than a single prop.
clusters.include: 'What parts make up X / how is it composed or operated / what does a complete usage look like / what props does it take' put to an Anatomy-type story not yet seen in source, including when the purpose is to weigh the component against another or when Anatomy is the only story offered.
clusters.exclude: Anatomy or leftover story mined mainly for native attributes, element type or submit ability -> k06. Anatomy chosen for its ARIA description -> k09. Asking for when-to-use guidance rather than structure -> k11. Story the trigger says was already seen, loaded again for what is inside -> k02. Unlisted, guessed story name -> k13.

clusters.label: Guessed story name for state wiring
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know how an overlay's open state is driven (open flag, close handler, content inside) but the docs list no story for it. It requests a story by a conventional state name ('Open') that was never listed, betting that such a story exists.
clusters.include: Loads of an unlisted, guessed story name in search of basic state wiring.
clusters.exclude: A listed structural story used for the same question -> k12.

clusters.label: Variant catalogue for available styles
clusters.definition: The component has no obvious variant prop and the agent needs to know which visual styles exist and which props or flags produce them (for instance a secondary look next to a primary one). It loads the 'Variants' story because the name promises every style side by side rather than one flag per story.
clusters.include: 'Which variants exist and how are they selected' put to a catalogue-style story.
clusters.exclude: How an in-context example pairs primary and secondary actions -> k01. Variants scanned for a functional (submit) variant -> k06. Custom restyling through className -> k15. Anatomy loaded to learn a component's basic props, even when hoping for a colour option -> k12.

clusters.label: className story as styling hook
clusters.definition: Built-in styles do not cover what the feature needs (distinct status colours, positioning a trigger), so the agent checks whether the component accepts a className and extra attributes as an escape hatch. It loads the 'Class Name' story because it is the one about custom styling hooks.
clusters.include: className / extra-attribute acceptance for the purpose of styling or positioning.
clusters.exclude: Class Name story read as evidence that non-style native attributes such as type pass through -> k06. Choosing among built-in variants -> k14.
